issues.problem: FAIL, context reversed. The words are an exact substring, but they are not the commenter's own view. The commenter then says 'The fact there is a home page which shows options similar to what I like is fine, sometimes useful. Yes I’d prefer to customise it. ... Option 1 (verified exact substring): “The breaking point for me was when I had to scroll past 3-4 rows of podcast suggestions (onto an entire other screen) to find any music on my homepage.” ([hacker-news, no rating, 2024-02-19](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39431191)); this commenter did quit over podcast pushing. If kept, reframe it honestly as a tunebox design requirement (show removed or unavailable tracks visibly rather than dropping them; one commenter stays with the original because it does this), using “Having the songs still appear lets me know, as it gives me the opportunity to find those songs elsewhere.” ([hacker-news, no rating, 2024-04-08](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39967357)). I understand the reasoning but it makes me irrationally angry” ([hacker-news, no rating, 2023-01-05](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=34259883)). issues.location: fixes.draft.md section 6, Angle A evidence line, and the Recommendation
issues.problem: '67 reviews across 3 sources' overstates A. The 67 are 59 HN comments plus 8 store rows. The other 11 are 4 requests for YouTube or SoundCloud content, 3 people moving catalogue playlists to another service, 3 ownership statements and 1 ambiguous row. issues.location: Section 6, Recommendation ('use B and C as the proof points') and Angle B
issues.problem: B's volume comes from people tunebox can't serve. 0 of the 116 free-tier-control reviewers own files: the only 2 owner-keyword hits both use 'my own song' to mean a chosen catalogue song. Aimed at mass-market listeners, B reads as free on-demand music, which is an implied catalogue promise. Nothing in either verified file shows a locker that mixes in songs, caps skips or gates controls. So against the alternatives owners actually weigh, the B proof points are parity.
issues.fix: Keep B as voice only. Replace the proof points with ones measured against lockers and self-hosting: zero setup with no server, whole-folder upload with originals kept (F6), always exportable but time-boxed (F7), and shuffle and history built for large collections (F4, F8). Treat F1 to F3 as hygiene.

issues.location: Section 6, Angle C
issues.problem: 26 of the 27 offline complaints concern the original's catalogue downloads; only 1 is about Local Files. For owners, the original's Local Files already play offline, YouTube Music uploads play offline without Premium (an HN user quoting Google's help page), and Plexamp has offline downloads (official listing). issues.location: F2 (Playlists play only what's in them) and its proposed features.csv row
issues.problem: The original already ships this, and the draft missed it. Premium can switch Smart Shuffle off (support article, 2026-05-13). Autoplay has an on/off switch on mobile and desktop, and its support article (updated 2025-09-25) shows no Premium label. The 2025-05-07 newsroom post says users can switch both off. Of 33 injection reviews I coded 16 free, 5 paying, 12 unknown. Of the 13 core reviews dated after 2026-05-13: 10 free, 3 unknown, 0 paying. So the draft's '13 of 25 after the article' reflects free users, for whom Smart Shuffle is always on by design; it does not show the fix failing.
issues.fix: Set the row to original = yes, with the note 'difference = default off'. Reword the date split to say 10 of those 13 are free-tier users. Label F2 hygiene, not a differentiator.

issues.location: F7 (Your library leaves with you) and its features.csv rows
issues.problem: 'The verified changelog shows no export' is true of that file but false of the product. The original's Download your data tool gives a ZIP of JSON with playlists (including local track names), Your Library, and lifetime streaming history (support articles, updated 2025-09-18 and 2026-07-07). The cited quote 14618139577 is a cancelled-Premium user whose downloaded catalogue greyed out, a catalogue and offline bug rather than owner lock-in. 'Playback stays on after cancel', original = no, is not like for like: the original's library stays playable on its free tier. Keeping playback and download open for people who stopped paying means storing 96 to 300 GB per 10,000-track library with no upper limit. A one-click export of the original files at that scale is M to L, not M.
issues.fix: Cite the original's data export and state what is left: on demand, M3U8/CSV, plus the audio files. Time-box post-cancel access (read-only plus export for N days, then deletion with notice). Drop the misfit quote and the 'original = no' post-cancel comparison. Replace 'never held hostage' with 'always exportable, with N days' notice before any deletion or shutdown'.

issues.location: F8 (Collector tools), proposed row 'Listening history page with play counts' (original = no)
issues.problem: The original already ships part of this: Recents (the last 50 songs on desktop, support 2025-06-30), a weekly listening snapshot (2025 recap), the lifetime-history export, Smart Filters, and playlists made from filtered Liked Songs (select markets). Navidrome shows play counts per user (official docs). Per-track play counts in the app were not found in the pages checked.
issues.fix: Mark history as original = partial. Claim only in-app per-track play counts and live-updating rule-based playlists as the difference, and note parity with Navidrome.

issues.location: F5 (Offline-first downloads) and the proposed row 'Single-track download and no expiry for own uploads'
issues.problem: The comparison is apples to oranges: for owned files, the original's Local Files sit on the device and work offline already, while the 30-day check-in applies to catalogue downloads. 'No expiry' also contradicts paid offline with plan re-checks. Making offline the paywall conflicts with YouTube Music's free offline uploads (user-quoting-official). The two official download-cap articles disagree ('on each of up to 5 devices' vs 'across up to 5 devices'), and the draft cites only one. 'Offline-first cuts egress' is only partly true, because whole-library downloads to several devices front-load egress.
issues.fix: Pick one model: (i) plain, non-expiring copies of the user's own files, with the paid part being sync convenience, or (ii) expiry after a lapse plus a grace period, without the word 'no expiry'. Compare against Local Files, YouTube Music uploads and Plexamp. Cite both cap wordings. Add /replica-launch for the in-app purchase rules and the pricing conflict, and cap the number of devices.

issues.location: F4 (A shuffle you can check), size S
issues.problem: Under-sized. A permutation on one device is S, but keeping the cycle across devices, surviving library edits mid-cycle, working with the user queue and shuffling a whole library of tens of thousands of tracks is M. PlaybackState is marked 'confidence: guess' in recon. The claim that the differentiators beat lockers is unsupported: the market file says nothing about how lockers shuffle.
issues.fix: Resize to M. Have /replica-architect specify PlaybackState before /replica-build and /replica-backend. Drop the comparison with lockers. Consider a 'spread artists' option and never market 'truly random'.

issues.location: F6 (The locker done right)
issues.problem: It is presented with differentiator framing, but it is table stakes. YouTube Music advertises uploads (official listing) and supports up to 100k (user-quoting-official). VOX keeps FLAC as FLAC with unlimited storage at $4.99/month, and iBroadcast uploads are free (official listings). 'Plexamp users complain of no M3U import' rests on one App Store review. The desktop watch-folder is a fourth client outside the web + iOS + Android scope. Of the 6 store upload rows, 4 want YouTube or SoundCloud content.
issues.fix: Label F6 'must, table stakes'. Write 'a Plexamp reviewer (thin)'. Move the desktop watch-folder out of v1 as a separate L. Have /replica-architect own the storage cost model for originals plus streaming copies.

issues.location: F1 (Every control on every plan)
issues.problem: The cited reviewers are free catalogue listeners, 0 of whom own files. Premium already has every one of these controls and markets them in its own words. Lockers don't gate controls. Mass-market copy like 'unlimited skips on every plan' implies free on-demand music. Making plans differ by offline downloads conflicts with YouTube Music's free offline uploads.
issues.fix: Keep it as an internal pricing and entitlement policy (S; /replica-launch plus /replica-backend), never as a headline or proof point. Avoid echoing the original's Premium wording. Settle the offline gate in /replica-launch.

issues.location: F3 (A quiet, music-only app)
issues.problem: It fits, since 'paying and still getting ads' (33) comes from payers and HN owners left over promo pop-ups. But it is table stakes against lockers: iBroadcast and Substreamer state 'no ads' in their official listings. 'Ad-free music' wording would imply ad-free commercial tracks. Rating prompts are thin (12, app-store only).
issues.fix: Keep it, framed as retention rather than acquisition. Use 'no ads in your library, on any plan', never 'ad-free music'.

issues.location: Legal notes (section 7) and features.csv sharing rows (Share a playlist by link, Public profile, Collaborative playlist)
issues.problem: Public streaming of uploaded audio to people who didn't upload it is the largest copyright exposure, and the evidence shows no demand for it: 0 owner requests to share their uploads, and 0 hits across all 1227 rows. 'Only among users who each own the tracks they add' can't be enforced. Background, not verified in this session: the EU DSM Directive Art. 2(6) excludes cloud services where users upload content for their own use from Art. 17, so public access may bring tunebox into scope; US §512(c) safe-harbour conditions apply; lockers that streamed uploads to others (MP3tunes, Grooveshark) were sued.
issues.fix: In v1, a share sends the tracklist only, and recipients play only tracks they uploaded themselves. Defer public profiles and collaborative audio. Review with counsel before launch.

issues.location: Quotes in sections 4 to 7 (all 24 are exact; the problem is fit)
issues.problem: U2 quote 39967357: the commenter likes that removed songs stay visible ('it's the reason I still use Spotify'). U3 quote 42113467 describes behaviour from about 2014 ('10 or so years ago'). The F1 and F2 quotes come from free-tier catalogue listeners. The F6 quote says Apple Music and YouTube Music already allow uploads, which is parity evidence.

issues.location: Section 1, 'All three lenses reached A independently'
issues.problem: True: fit.md, market.md and evidence.md each recommend A. But all three coded the same HN-heavy, ownership-searched sample, so their agreement is not independent market evidence. The draft also rejects the Subsonic API as 'HN-only, thin' while accepting A, whose upload demand is equally HN-only (59 of 67).

issues.location: Section 7, pricing notes for /replica-launch
issues.problem: Missing two signals. 4 owners are subscription-averse (HN 3, app-store 1; thin). 6 HN owners are gap-fillers who want uploads alongside a catalogue, which Apple Music and YouTube Music already provide and tunebox can't. Free competitors (YouTube Music uploads, iBroadcast) cap the price near zero.
issues.fix: Add both signals. Test storage-based or one-time pricing next to the subscription.

issues.location: Absolute claims across F5, F7 and Angles A and C
issues.problem: 'Never disappear', 'never held hostage', 'never lets you down', 'no expiry' and 'plays untouched' are absolute. Streams are transcoded on lower plans (F6), so 'untouched' holds only for the stored copy. Lockers have a history of shutting down.
issues.fix: Use bounded, policy-backed wording: 'stored copy kept bit for bit', 'always exportable, with N days' notice', and the DMCA caveat.

notes.quotes:
The draft does not pass: 3 quotes fail on context and 3 more need a short note added.

notes.fit:
The draft fails this check as written. None of the fixes promises catalogue access, ad-free commercial music or artist payouts, and the plan is mostly buildable. But four things need fixing:

1. **Angle A is overstated.** In substance its evidence is HN-only. On my reading, 1 of the 12 store rows in the own-files themes is about owned files, and none of the 1088 store reviews clearly asks to upload files the reviewer owns.
2. **The B and C proof points come from catalogue listeners.** 0 of 116 free-tier reviewers own files, and 26 of 27 offline complaints are about the original's catalogue downloads. Against the alternatives owners actually name (Apple Music 15, Plex 12, YouTube Music 11, Navidrome 8, Jellyfin 6, iBroadcast 0, VOX 1) they are parity.
3. **The original already ships things the draft missed.** For F2: Smart Shuffle off for Premium, and an Autoplay switch with no Premium label. For F7: a Download your data export with playlists and lifetime history. For F8: Recents and the weekly snapshot. I fetched 4 new official support pages on 2026-10-04 to confirm these.
4. **Size and claim errors.** F4 is M, not S. F5's "no expiry" contradicts paid offline. F6's desktop watch-folder is a fourth client. F7's post-cancel access has no storage cap.

**Strongest counter-case:** keep A as the category, because it is the only angle where buyer and product match. Aim it at would-be self-hosters and former Google Play Music users, with proof points measured against lockers and self-hosting. Make the waitlist test a gate. Keep a Subsonic-compatible API in view as a feasibility hedge for mobile offline.

**Method:** keyword nets only found candidates; I read every one in full and coded it by hand (one coder, no second rater). That covers injection (33), offline (27) and shuffle (25), the owner-signal hits, and all 12 store rows in the own-files themes. All 37 quotes in verify-fit.md pass the machine check. Reddit, Trustpilot and the community board were not reached.

**Unverified items:** a few legal and platform points are background knowledge, marked as unverified in the report: EU DSM Art. 2(6)/Art. 17, US §512(c), the MP3tunes and Grooveshark cases, App Store metadata rules, and OS cache purging.
